description:
Going beyond personal grief, the story explores profound themes of memory and forgetting, the nature of time, and the unwavering love of parents who refuse to give up on their children. Set against the vastness of space and a science-fiction backdrop, the work combines the author's distinctive, bold artwork with his deeply humanistic perspective, already evident in his previous works exploring historical suffering and the weight of human existence.

Amid immense sorrow, Park delicately portrays the enduring power of human compassion and hope, leaving readers with a deeply moving story and profound questions. More than a science-fiction adventure, Paradise invites us to reflect on the value of memory and the meaning of human dignity in an age defined by loss.
